result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep fast loads silent, use a 300ms threshold and handle failure well with the old results kept, a plain-language banner and Retry. A wins narrowly because it never removes the stale results and limits skeletons to the first load. B swaps the dimmed cards for skeletons after 1.5s, which hides useful content and adds a second swap that can cause layout shift. B does mark loading more clearly on the map with its floating pill and adds useful extras like automatic retry and a 10s timeout. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep stale content visible, use timing thresholds and specify a strong failure state with a plain-language banner and Retry. B is more consistent. It never swaps stale results for skeletons, keeps skeletons for the first load only, reserves space for the error banner and animates only opacity and transform. A replaces the dimmed cards with skeletons after 1.5s, which partly blanks the previous results. A does have a more explicit map-side indicator and failure notice.
